protocolos.resumen: A crew member has a red light on pulse, oxygen, or breathing. You are not the medic: your job is to call, secure, and stay.
protocolos.prioridad: Crew trigger card · escalate to the CMO
protocolos.equipoUbicacion: Voice loop: intercom channel 2 · PBA mask: forward bulkhead · Handrail and harness: any node
protocolos.fuente: Adapted for non-medical crew from NASA HRP cardiovascular risks. [TO BE VALIDATED]

pasos.instruccion: Open the voice loop and say the crew member's name and which light is red: pulse, oxygen, or breathing.
pasos.nota0G: Say the numbers you see on screen, not what you think they mean.

pasos.titulo: Help the crew member stay still
pasos.instruccion: In microgravity nobody falls, they float. Clip the crew member to a handrail or harness so they cannot drift.
pasos.nota0G: A drifting patient pulls the oxygen line and the sensor cable with them.

pasos.instruccion: Ask about chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness, and report the answer to the CMO.
pasos.nota0G: Stay within arm's reach and keep talking; confusion is a symptom, not a mood.

pasos.instruccion: If the oxygen light is red, put the PBA mask on the crew member's face and ask them to breathe normally.
pasos.nota0G: Seal the mask before you look for the cause of the alarm.

pasos.titulo: Repeat the reading with new hardware
pasos.instruccion: Measure again with a new sensor or cartridge to rule out an equipment error before anyone decides.
pasos.nota0G: A single red reading is a question, not a diagnosis.

protocolos.resumen: The cabin CO2 reading is climbing. Reduce the source, restore the air, and log the value.
protocolos.prioridad: Crew trigger card · escalate to the CMO
protocolos.equipoUbicacion: CO2 display: environmental rack · Scrubber status: cabin panel · PBA mask: forward bulkhead
protocolos.fuente: Adapted from NASA HRP closed and hostile environment hazards (cabin CO2). [TO BE VALIDATED]

pasos.titulo: Read the CO2 value out loud
pasos.instruccion: Say the exact number on the display to the CMO, not a range and not an impression.
pasos.nota0G: CO2 pockets form where ventilation is weak; the sensor position matters.

pasos.instruccion: Ask the whole crew to slow down: less movement means less CO2 produced in the same volume.
pasos.nota0G: Exercise on orbit can double CO2 production for the whole module.

pasos.instruccion: Confirm that the scrubber and filters are running and that no alarm is latched on the panel.
pasos.nota0G: A filter that is on but saturated moves air without removing CO2.

pasos.titulo: Use the portable mask if it keeps rising
pasos.instruccion: If the level does not fall, put on the PBA mask while the atmosphere recovers.
pasos.nota0G: The mask buys time; it does not fix the cabin.

pasos.instruccion: Store the value in the deferred queue so it travels to ground control with the next synchronization.
pasos.nota0G: The queue keeps the timestamp even if the console loses power.

protocolos.resumen: The dosimeter shows a cumulative dose above the crew limit. Shield the crew member and record the number.
protocolos.prioridad: Crew trigger card · escalate to the Flight Surgeon
protocolos.equipoUbicacion: Dosimeter display: crew console · Shielded zone: service module aft
protocolos.fuente: Adapted from NASA HRP space radiation hazards. [TO BE VALIDATED]

pasos.instruccion: Say the dose on screen to the CMO with its unit and the period it covers.
pasos.nota0G: Cumulative dose is a career number; a single reading is not the whole story.

pasos.titulo: Move to the most shielded zone
pasos.instruccion: Move the crew member to the area with the thickest shielding and keep them there.
pasos.nota0G: Water and equipment racks are shielding: put mass between the crew and the source.

pasos.titulo: Cut exposure time and log it
pasos.instruccion: Reduce the time spent in the exposed area and record the reading for the next synchronization.
pasos.nota0G: Dose is rate multiplied by time: leaving early is the intervention.

protocolos.titulo: Metabolic change in the lab panel
protocolos.resumen: One analyte left its reference range. Confirm the sample before anyone acts on it.
protocolos.prioridad: Crew trigger card · escalate to the Flight Surgeon
protocolos.equipoUbicacion: Blood analyzer: lab rack · Baseline: personal OSD-575 record · Cartridges: lab drawer
protocolos.fuente: NASA OSDR OSD-575 reference ranges plus a non-medical crew adaptation. [TO BE VALIDATED]

pasos.instruccion: Run a new cartridge to confirm the value before acting on it.
pasos.nota0G: A used cartridge or a short sample is the most common false alarm.

pasos.instruccion: Look at your baseline on screen: the app already compares it. Yellow is an alert, not an emergency.
pasos.nota0G: Your normal is not the population average; it is your own curve.

pasos.titulo: Tell the CMO the value and the drift
pasos.instruccion: Report the value and how far it moved from your normal, not just whether it is high or low.
pasos.nota0G: A small drift over weeks can matter more than one outlier.

pasos.titulo: Queue the reading for the Flight Surgeon
pasos.instruccion: Store the result so the queue sends it to the Flight Surgeon when the link returns.
pasos.nota0G: Deferred synchronization is the normal path, not a failure.
